question: NO2 in Athens, Greece

In March 2023, the Court of Justice of the European Union ruled1 that from 2010 until 2020 Greece had systematically and persistently failed to keep nitrogen dioxide (NO2) levels in the agglomeration of Athens2 under the annual limit values established in Directive 2008/50/EC3 and that it had breached its obligation to ensure that air quality plans4 are established and provide for appropriate measures to keep the exceedance period as short as possible.

Taking into consideration that, according to the data reported5, the exceedance of the annual limit in the agglomeration of Athens persisted in 2021 and 2022 and that the infringement procedure is still active: 1.

Has the Greek government, since the ruling, adopted and communicated remedial measures to rectify the exceedance and comply with the provisions of the Directive, in particular those pertaining to the NO2limit values and the establishment of air quality plans with appropriate measures?
What concrete measures has the Commission taken since the ruling to ensure the Member State complies with the provisions of the directive?

Judgment of the Court of Justice of 16 February 2023, Commission v Greece (ECLI:EU:C:2023:112). Zone EL0003. Directive 2008/50/EC of 21 May 2008 on ambient air quality and cleaner air for Europe (OJ L 152, 11.6.2008, p. 1), Article 13 and Annex IX. Article 23(1) of Directive 2008/50 read in conjunction with Section A of Annex XV. https://tableaupublic.discomap.eea.europa.eu/views/attainment_ng/Master?%3Aembed=y&%3AisGuestRedirectFromVizpor tal=y.
answer: Following the ruling of the Court of Justice of the EU of 16 February 2023 (Case C-633/21) the Greek authorities have communicated a list of measures that are being planned or are being implemented in order to comply with the ruling of the Court.
The Commission will continue to closely monitor the situation in order to ensure that the Court ruling is complied with as soon as possible and, if necessary, will not hesitate to take further steps.

In line with a judgment of the Court on a similar case (6), should the Commission deem it necessary to send a Letter of Formal Notice under Article 260 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU in the present infringement case, such letter must rely on data gathered after the delivery of the ruling.
The Commission should receive such data from Greece in September 2024 and will thereafter consider the need and timing of any further action.

In a case against Bulgaria (ruling of 16 March 2023 in Case C-174/21 for the non-execution of the ruling of 5 April 2017 in Case C-488/15) regarding the exceedances of particulate matter10 limit values, the Court declared the infringement action of the Commission as inadmissible, because the Letter of Formal Notice that had been sent following the first ruling was based on monitoring data that covered the years preceding the delivery of the first ruling.
